subject: Customer latency blitz — request for exec prioritization & mitigation roadmap
body:
-----Original Message-----
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Executive Ops <execops@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Customer latency blitz — request for exec prioritization & mitigation roadmap

Team —

Quick summary up front: CardinalPay (priority enterprise, Reserved Capacity contract) is seeing a simultaneous latency & 5xx spike across their production inference pool starting ~03:00 UTC this morning. Token latency has jumped from baseline 120ms p50 to ~1.2s p50 and 5xx rate climbed to ~3.7% (baseline <0.2%). Throughput saturation observed on their dedicated GPU pool; our telemetry shows continuous queue growth and repeated fallback to the small-variant model which is also hitting limits.

Attached: slo-impact-matrix.xlsx (high level customer-facing SLO impact) and capture-logs-20270925.tar.gz (sampling of request traces and kernel logs).

Immediate asks:
- Exec prioritization to allow emergency reserved-capacity increase for CardinalPay (they are on a 12-month reserved plan; committed throughput mismatch here is causing customer-visible errors).
- Approve temporary throttle on non-essential background requests routed to the same pool (CS & SRE to coordinate).
- Ops: short-term mitigation — scale up dedicated pool by +8 GPUs in us-west-2 for next 48 hours, run canary that drops model size to the quantized-x2 variant for high-latency call paths.

Why this needs exec attention: CardinalPay is in active negotiation for a multi-month expansion (deal D-49321). If we don't stabilize within the next 24–36 hours they will trigger their contractual SLA review and consider temporary failover to another vendor for critical flows. This has both revenue and reference risk.

Telemetry snapshot (top-level):
- window 02:45–08:00 UTC: queue depth at pool +220% vs baseline, average token latency p50->p95 increased from 120/300ms to 1.2s/3.4s.
- error profile: 5xx spikes correlated with GPU kernel retries and out-of-memory evictions on node set rd-pool-34.
- routing: 72% of CardinalPay traffic hitting dedicated pool; fallbacks to small-variant model increased rate by 28% in same window.

Suggested short timeline (proposed by ops):
- T+0–2h: Approve emergency capacity commit; apply traffic-weighted request throttles; open live incident bridge.
- T+2–8h: Add +8 GPUs, enable KV cache warming and prefix caching for high-volume endpoints; deploy quantized-x2 canary for 10% of traffic.
- T+8–36h: Monitor SLOs; if stable, plan for dedicated reserved increase and postmortem to update routing/rate-limit policies.

Please advise with an "approve" or "decline" and any changes to the timeline. If approved, I will open the procurement/ops change and loop in CS to communicate to CardinalPay.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior AM, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

-----Original Reply-----
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 09:46:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer latency blitz — request for exec prioritization & mitigation roadmap

Naomi —
Acknowledged. I'll get infra to validate the OOM patterns on rd-pool-34 and confirm whether the kernel retries are symptomatic of a memory regression vs hotspot load. Short questions:
1) Can we get a 1-hour snapshot of per-node GPU utilization and current queued token backlog?
2) Do we have any available spare GPUs in us-west-2 we can hot-add immediately, or does that require capacity reallocation from other pools?

If infra confirms node-level memory pressure, I support the +8 GPUs immediate add and a canary to quantized-x2. I will stand up a bridge with ops and include SRE.

-David

-----Original Message from Priya Sethi -----
From: Priya Sethi <priya@cardinalpay.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: CardinalPay SRE <sre@cardinalpay.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 11:02:38 +0000
Subject: Re: Production errors / latency — CardinalPay

Naomi —
Thanks for flagging. Our payments-microservice saw intermittent 500s starting at ~02:50 UTC and users experienced checkout failures for ~90 minutes. We temporarily rerouted lower-priority requests and reduced batch sizes which helped, but the root cause looks like model-side queueing across your dedicated pool. We need a firm remediation plan and timeline — this impacts our compliance reporting and merchant SLA. Please escalate on your side.

Regards,
Priya Sethi
Head of Platform Engineering, CardinalPay

-----Reply from Vivek Kulkarni-----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer latency blitz — request for exec prioritization & mitigation roadmap

Team —
I want to be clear: get me the emergency capacity request in writing and CC execs. I will approve an emergency reserved-capacity bump for CardinalPay for up to 72 hours provided we have the following:
- Ops run immediate hot-add of GPU capacity in us-west-2 (+8 GPUs).
- Product to enable temporary fallback to quantized-x2 only for high-latency endpoints (canary 10% -> 50% ramp if stable).
- Engineering to produce a 24h post-incident plan that includes root cause hypothesis, scheduling for a non-emergency permanent capacity adjustment, and a rollback plan if quantized variant degrades accuracy beyond agreed thresholds.

Please treat this as priority; CC me when the change request is filed.
Vivek

-----Final consolidation from Naomi Feldman-----
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Priya Sethi <priya@cardinalpay.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer latency blitz — request for exec prioritization & mitigation roadmap

Update and action summary (24h):
- Incident bridge opened Fri 09:55 PDT.
- Infra confirmed node-level memory pressure and kernel retry cascade on rd-pool-34.
- Ops hot-added +8 GPUs in us-west-2 at Fri 11:20 PDT (temporary commit).
- Product deployed quantized-x2 canary (10% traffic) at Fri 13:00 PDT; early metrics show p50 latency improved from 1.2s -> 420ms on canary traffic.
- From a customer comms perspective, Priya: we acknowledge impact, committed to the following: full postmortem by Tue EOD, provisional reserved-capacity increase for 72 hours (approved by Vivek), and a technical deep-dive with your SREs Monday morning.

Pending items / owners:
- Engineering (David): deliver root cause hypothesis and remediation ETA (Mon 10:00 PDT).
- Product (Naomi): finalize procurement change and bill-of-materials for long-term reserved increase (Mon 12:00 PDT).
- CS (Naomi): coordinate customer-facing incident summary and SL offering.

I will attach the postmortem and usage delta when available. Thanks for the quick coordination — we'll continue to monitor and report hourly until the queue stabilizes.

Naomi Feldman
Senior AM, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

-- Attachment stubs:
1) slo-impact-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
2) capture-logs-20270925.tar.gz (logs archive)

-- Incident bridge link: https://redwood.app/console/incident/INC-78233
